Let me think about this year like I always do.

My land is only 4.1 mu, not big. I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for many years, same as my neighbors in the village. Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize maybe 520 kg. Not bad, not great. I will do mostly the same this year — changing too much is risky, and fertilizer and seed cost real money.

For wheat: I will plant Jimai 22, same variety my neighbor Old Wang uses and he gets good yield. Seeds from the town agro-shop. For fertilizer, I put two bags of compound fertilizer (diammonium, about 50 jin each) before plowing — that gives me the base. Then in spring when wheat turns green, I put urea, maybe 15-20 kg per mu on top. Total nitrogen about 16 kg per mu I think. I water 4 times: before winter, at greening, at jointing, and when grain is filling. If I skip water at jointing the yield drops, I learned that before. Aphids come in May so I spray at least twice, plus once for rust if I see yellow spots. I use rotary tiller — the tractor man charges by mu, not expensive.

For maize: I plant Zhengdan 958, it is reliable. Everyone in our village plants hybrid maize now, nobody uses old seeds. After wheat harvest in June I just drill the maize directly, no-till — saves time and money, and the wheat stubble keeps moisture. I put compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at big trumpet stage (around 15 kg per mu). Nitrogen maybe 17 kg total because maize is hungry. If July and August rain enough I only water once, otherwise twice from my well. Corn borer always comes, I spray once or twice.

My family has 4 people, some work outside, so labor is mostly me and my wife. I cannot afford to lose a harvest — better to put a little extra fertilizer than save money and get poor yield. Small farm like mine, every mu must produce.
